clue.text: Presumably, you are pre-tax?

parts.note: if you are the 'pre' part of the word, the speaker must be the 'post' part, and together the speaker's 'I am post' names a levy

explanation.surface: Someone muses about a salary figure before deductions are taken.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M POST: if you are pre, I am post. The whole thing also names a tax, especially one on imports.
explanation.definitionFit: An impost is a duty or levy, especially a customs charge on imported goods.

clue.text: Bad time (it's admitted) to be a god

indicators.note: letting in means the time goes inside the bad word

parts.note: immoral means bad

explanation.surface: An awful moment lets someone in, to be made divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' puts T inside IMMORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gods of myth never die, so a deity is called one who lives for ever.

clue.text: Shepard's blasted off, so it's said

indicators.note: blasted off suggests the name is blown apart and reassembled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Astronaut Alan Shepard was launched into space, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blasted' rearranges SHEPARD; the possessive 's gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something phrased has been put into words, as a remark worded a certain way.

clue.text: Given sudden emphasis, what can make zoo so?

parts.note: the change from the animal park word to the short adverb is made by putting S in place of Z, and dropping an O

explanation.surface: Someone asks how 'zoo' could be turned into 'so' with a sudden stress.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as S FOR Z AND O: put S in place of Z and drop one O, and ZOO becomes SO. Taken whole, it is the musical marking.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning a note or chord is played with sudden strong accent.

clue.text: Slow mover in France is carrying burden

indicators.note: the French word holds the load inside it, as a vehicle carries freight

parts.note: est is French for 'is'
a burden or load is cargo

explanation.surface: Something sluggish in France is lugging a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' looks like part of the definition of a French snail, but it belongs to the wordplay: it makes 'is' French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a snail, a creature famous for crawling slowly, eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Gauging the amount of reaction, long-suffering one enters residence with no end of deception

parts.note: a stoic endures hardship without complaint

indicators.note: the one goes into the residence

parts.note: home is a residence
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: no end of means the deception word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trick is a deception

explanation.surface: A patient chemist moves house while measuring how much of a reaction there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts I in HOME; 'with no end of' cuts TRICK to TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the quantitative proportions in which substances react in chemistry.

clue.text: Where we will vow to announce change

indicators.note: announcing means saying out loud, so we want a word sounding like change

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A couple plan to declare a change in where they marry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to announce' signals a homophone of ALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedding vows are traditionally exchanged before the altar of a church.

clue.text: Single sign young woman's got over eminent scientist

indicators.note: in a down entry, being over means the girl comes above the other pieces

parts.note: gal is a young woman
I is the Roman numeral one, single
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A girl born under a single star sign has outshone a great scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' means above, so the girl sits on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer and physicist famous for his telescope.

clue.text: Formidable person raising vermin

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: vermin here means rodents, two rats

explanation.surface: A fearsome character breeds rats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' reverses RAT RAT, two of the vermin, upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartar is a fierce or intractable person, from the Tatar warriors.

clue.text: They'll save American lives once mustard gas gets dispersed

indicators.note: a gas spreading out scatters, so the letters are scattered and regrouped

explanation.surface: Lifesavers come to the rescue when a wartime gas cloud clears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets dispersed' rearranges ONCE MUSTARD GAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Coast Guard's members rescue people in danger at sea.

clue.text: Traveller gets discharge in second game

indicators.note: the electrical flash sits inside the short word for a brief moment

parts.note: MO is short for a moment, a second
an arc is an electrical discharge across a gap
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A traveller suffers some leakage partway through a match.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, a moment, is everyday British slang for a second, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian merchant famous for his journey to the court of Kublai Khan.

clue.text: Roof worker landed again from the East

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: birds that relit have landed again

explanation.surface: A roofer touched down once more after flying in from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' reverses RELIT, as an across entry is read from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lays roofing slates or clay tiles works on roofs.

clue.text: Sleeveless dress one with endless relish adjusts to fit

indicators.note: losing its sleeves, the word dress loses its outer letters at either side

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: without its end, the word for relish drops its final letter

parts.note: zest is relish or enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A tailor alters a sleeveless frock with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeveless' leaves RES from dress; 'endless' turns ZEST into ZES.
explanation.definitionFit: To change the size of something, as a garment or image is altered to fit.

clue.text: All the petals curl inside short envelope

indicators.note: the coil of the curl is placed within the shortened covering
short means the covering word loses its last letter

parts.note: a coat is an outer covering or envelope
to curl up is to roll

explanation.surface: Petals curl up within a little casing, like a bud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the petals' reads like a description, but it is a botanical definition of a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical term for the whole ring of petals of a flower, taken together.

clue.text: Universal study, in pursuit of a poet

indicators.note: chasing after means the universal study comes behind the letter a

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Universal study chases after a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pursuit of' puts U and DEN after A.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was a major Anglo-American poet of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Dodgy behaviour? He's fleeing the nest!

definitions.meaning: read as a boy leaving home, the phrase splits into a departing male child

explanation.surface: A parent tuts at shady conduct as their boy moves out.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as GOING, SON: a son who is leaving home.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on is an idiom for questionable or improper conduct.

clue.text: Wedding attendant's cryptic monograms

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are jumbled into a disguised form

explanation.surface: A wedding helper is behind the puzzling embroidered initials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges MONOGRAMS; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A groomsman attends the bridegroom at a wedding, a male usher.

clue.text: Plan in gallery — get art set up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
in means the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A scheme in the gallery to get the artworks installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside the words; 'up' reads YGETARTS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a plan of action designed to reach a goal.

clue.text: Ages getting into state of matter, but not a superfluous word

indicators.note: the long period goes inside the shortened matter state
but not tells us to leave out the letter named next

parts.note: plasma is the fourth state of matter after solid, liquid and gas
an eon is an immense age

explanation.surface: Eras slip into a physical phase, though without a word too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not a' drops the final A of PLASMA, giving PLASM; 'getting into' puts EON in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleonasm is the use of redundant words, as in 'free gift'.

clue.text: Attractive woman flowers after learning

indicators.note: the flowers come behind the learning

parts.note: lore is traditional learning
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers

explanation.surface: A charming woman blooms after study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' might suggest a river, but here it is the Hawaiian garland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the Rhine siren who lured sailors, hence any alluring woman.

clue.text: Start operating TV?

parts.note: a machine that is on is operating
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the way to start is by switching on the television.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means the beginning, as of an illness or of winter.

clue.text: Whip a couple of scrambled eggs

indicators.note: a couple of means the first two letters of the next word

parts.note: two eggs: O, egg-shaped, and URGE, to egg on

explanation.surface: Beat a pair of scrambled eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of' takes SC from scrambled. The eggs are two: O for its shape, and URGE, as to egg someone on.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip used to inflict punishment.

clue.text: He doubted he would get zero in maths after revision

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the subject
revision means reworking, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: O is zero

explanation.surface: He was sceptical that he'd score nought in maths even after revising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O into MATHS; 'after revision' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Thomas doubted the Resurrection until he saw the wounds.

clue.text: Coloured, perhaps — grabbing bishop, one didn't stop to think?

indicators.note: the coloured word clutches the bishop and the one inside it

parts.note: hued means coloured
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A painter seizes a bishop in a rush, without pausing for thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coloured, perhaps' hints that HUED is only one way of saying coloured; 'one' is not part of the definition but the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rushed or acted in haste failed to pause for reflection.

clue.text: Perfect drugs? Negotiate with me!

parts.note: I is the word for me, the speaker
to deal is both to sell drugs and to bargain

explanation.surface: A dealer offers perfect drugs and invites haggling.
explanation.walkthrough: The dealer's own words read I DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means perfect, the best one could imagine.

clue.text: Order book many sent back covering lottery

indicators.note: the reversed word wraps round the order and the book
sent back means the word for many is read in reverse

parts.note: a lot means many
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Ordering a book, many are returned with a raffle ticket attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns A LOT into TOLA; 'covering' puts OM and B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle where tickets are drawn from a spinning drum, a kind of lottery.

clue.text: Heading for Newcastle, a long way to go round for AA

indicators.note: the distance wraps round the initial letter of the city

parts.note: a mile is a long way

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for' gives N; 'to go round' puts MILE around it. AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring breakdown service, but here A. A. are initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne wrote Winnie-the-Pooh, so his initials stand for the author.

clue.text: Newspaper just installs good printing software

explanation.walkthrough: 'installs' puts G inside MERE. The Mail is the Daily Mail, a British newspaper.

clue.text: Until 197l, ready here to make notes about eminence

indicators.note: the singing goes around the high ground

parts.note: to sing is to make musical notes
an eminence is a hill or piece of high ground

explanation.surface: A banker plans to write notes about a prominent figure from before 1971.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is slang for cash; until decimalisation in 1971 Britain had a coin worth twelve old pence, a twentieth of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A British coin used before decimal money arrived, so it was ready cash in Britain then.

clue.text: One of seven miners given to outbursts

definitions.meaning: one of the dwarfs who mine in the Snow White story
prone to sudden explosive fits, as of sneezes

explanation.walkthrough: The dwarfs in Disney's Snow White work in a mine.
